title: Brief Stock Market Update + When To Sell
description: Picked up a new stock this morning...
body_html:
In 2021, I downloaded TikTok to simply check out a dairy farm’s videos down the road. Naturally, the TikTok algorithm figured out I was an investor and began feeding me crypto and stock videos. Every video I saw was “BUY BUY BUY”. At the same time, I was selling off my 2018 & 2019 crypto and stock purchases, capturing some life changing profits. The videos screaming to “buy” were making me incredibly agitated 😡. As I sat in a crypto streamers live, rolling my eyes, I commented in the chat about “when to sell”, something about divergences. He said in the stream: “you should make a video”… and so, I did.

I never intended to become a finance content creator, it just kind of happened and today I have over 576,000 followers (TikTok is deactivated…I take breaks when I want to). My earliest videos were all about crypto crashing, Ethereum plummeting and that assets like Safemoon were not actually safe. I received an enormous amount of hate. Literally thousands of hate comments. I nearly quit, never to make a video again. Hate is engagement though, which only caused the videos to actually go more viral.

About 2 weeks later, crypto experienced its first massive drawdown, some assets crashing more than -80%. The hate comments got quiet. The top buyers were holding bags. And thus my reputation for reliability grew. It was further corroborated when I sold my stocks off in August of 2021…in which the market fell more than -27% for nearly a year in 2022.

Oddly I have a reputation for being a bear… maybe because those videos go more viral than my bullish ones. People literally fear when I post a bearish video, because I have a very high accuracy hit rate with tops. Regardless, I am more of a “skeptical bull”… more 95% of my profits come from going long. I only short in very particular environments with high confidence set ups. But there are several subtle clues for tops, and I will share those down below. asked for this on my post about Tesla, Stop Analysis and Position Sizing, and I think many people would benefit.

But first, how’s the market looking this week!?

Our silver miner stock, is leading the charge this week, up a little over 9% today. My positions can be found in the StockTok Summary. Its also where I share screener results, a niche python screener I built that finds the top 5 best stocks for both mid-term and long-term investments, daily. I also picked up the The Stock I mentioned Friday. Ping me in the Main Chat if you have any questions.

Most stocks look fairly bullish. Many have great volatility contraction patterns on them…I’ve mentioned this before, if we were to be approaching a bear market, we would not see so many bullish patterns. Its unlikely that ALL of those stocks are lying to us. Additionally, the S&P 500 has been shrugging off negative news since April 8th, when we shifted from “do nothing” to “buy” again. I fully expect more all time highs to from the major indexes, and multiple individual names. I remain bearish on oil.

I don’t like to boast or brag, as markets love to humble big ego’s…but here is how the calls are aging:

If things should change, as always I will update you.

But now back to the main topic, when to sell:

Lets establish what is most important first. The entire point of investing or trading, is to make money.

  • Not to call tops

  • Not to buy the bottom

  • Not to be “right”

Michael Burry continues to be one of the absolute worst investors on Substack…why? Because he is more attached to narratives, and being “right,” than he is price action. His portfolio has been in constant decline since 2021. Why people continue to subscribe to him, besides his one hit wonder movie…I’ll never understand.

Whether you are a day trader using the 5 minute chart, or a long term investor, holding positions for years… you must click the sell button at some point, and realize profits. Again, the point is to make money. About 99% of the “diamond hands” people I meet…end up holding into extreme losses. “Diamond hands” is one of the most toxic buzz phrases in the finance world, in my opinion.

So when do I decide to click sell?

There are 3 primary clues I most often use, and I’ll go through these in order of least preferred to most preferred.

#3 - The Stock Circle Jerk (Least Preferred)

This is a more recent strategy, as being a content creator has its benefits. I can see what thousands of people are thinking, particularly retail investors, on an individual stock, through comments, social media posts, likes, etc. Its classic “shoe shine boy” situation, at scale. The "shoeshine boy" story is a famous 1929 market anecdote where Joseph P. Kennedy Sr. allegedly decided to sell all his stocks after a shoeshine boy offered him hot stock tips. Kennedy reasoned that if "uninformed" public participants were heavily invested, the market was in a dangerous bubble.

A recent example was Netflix, back in October, I noticed there was “circle jerking” on TikTok. Several creators were posting bullish “up forever” posts. The comments were egotistically confident. When I posted that Netflix was getting hot, just like crypto in 2021, I received hundreds of angry, hateful, emotionally charged comments. And that’s when I knew…Netflix was done. Netflix from time of post to trough, dropped nearly -40%.

I actually appreciate hate comments, in mass, now that it has become such a reliable signal. When I see a circle jerk over a stock going on…its likely done.

You do not need to be a creator for this signal. Simply go to TikTok, or YouTube or even X. Search your stock…and I hate to say it like this, but its the truth: if you see degenerate dweebs with huge egos, especially if they have ridiculous price targets: you got yourself a great inverse indication.

#2 - Multiple Bearish Divergences (Preferred)

For those that are more technical, bearish divergences, particularly ones with multiple peaks and troughs, are another reliable indication. Normally I do not use indicators and invest/trade completely with naked charts (no indicators)…but I do throw RSI up to simply see if divergences are forming. A divergence is a mismatch between price action (higher highs/lower lows) and indicator action.

One of my more famous and successful shorts was Cardano (this works for stocks and crypto). Cardano dropped more than -90%. As an example, we can see on the weekly chart, that the price action was getting higher, yet the RSI, was forming lower highs. It is highly preferable, and more reliable, that you get multiple divergences and an actual break in price action downwards, to confirm the move. Single divergence (when you would just draw 2 of those red circles) is less reliable than when you draw 3 or 4 of those signals going down on the lagging indicator.

Also note, the longer the time frame is, the more reliable the divergence is. Its also optimal to wait for an actual break in price action downwards. You do not need to short or sell the top… just need to avoid the down trend.

#1 - The “Oh Shit” Candle (Most Preferred)

This is my most preferred method. Price action is the single best indicator for the markets. Period. December 19th I posted that the stock market was going to crash. At the time, I did not know how big the crash would be…whether it would be -20% or -80%. But I had a good idea that it would be better to NOT hold during that time, regardless of severity or duration. Note: I switched back to bullish June 2025 and have remained a bull since.

An “oh shit” candle is a term I came up with, but its simple. If you see devastating price action, relative to a single day, its a very reliable signal that big money is starting to cash out. Something is not normal. Maybe you don’t know what that something is…but big money knows something you don’t. You will literally find yourself saying: “OH SHIT”

I posted the bearish video, because a single day candle, had just wiped away more than a month’s worth of bullish price action. The FOMC back then acted as the catalyst. Its also an indication that price action was reacting bearish to news… a trend that can go on for a while.

“Oh shit” candles can be bullish as well. It was the primary clue that the bull market was back in mid 2025.

Notice in how all of these trades, I never caught a top. Never caught a bottom. Never predicted when or where they would land (I hate price targets…such a waste of time and energy). But I have been able to consistently ride trends. Then…, all I have to do is slap a stop into profit and, eventually, REALIZE PROFIT. The point is to make money, not “be right” or “predict the top”.

Are these methods perfect? No. There is no perfect method. There is no 100% reliability for anything. But these are fairly simple strategies that you can integrate into your strategy, and timeframe of trading and investing. No crystal ball required.

As always, if you have questions, ping me in the Main Chat. Also don’t forget to check out the stock I picked up this morning, found in the StockTok Summary and chat quick notes.

Thanks for stopping by!
